instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. A team builds a new feature that answers requests for the path /convert. The team wants a serverless solution, so that no instances need to be managed for this feature. The requests and the responses are small JSON documents. The rest of the application must stay unchanged. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that receives the requests for the path from the load balancer and invokes the AWS Lambda function for each request.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with a target group of type lambda, register the AWS Lambda function, and send the requests for the path to it.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a target group of type lambda, register the AWS Lambda function in it, and add a listener rule that forwards the path to the target group.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Gateway Load Balancer in front of the AWS Lambda function, and route the requests for the path through a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an internet-facing Application Load Balancer that has its own security group. A security audit finds that the instances are in public subnets with public IP addresses. Their security group allows HTTP on port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. The company must stop all direct access to the instances from the internet. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with each EC2 instance, and add a rule that blocks every request that does not come from the load balancer.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a network ACL for the instance subnets that allows inbound HTTP only from the current IP addresses of the load balancer, found with a DNS lookup.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the security group of the instances so that it allows HTTP only from the security group of the load balancer, and remove the 0.0.0.0/0 rule.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the instances in public subnets with public IP addresses, and allow HTTP in their security group only from the CIDR block of the VPC.

options.label: E
options.text: Move the instances to private subnets, launch them without public IP addresses, and keep them registered in the target group of the load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Sometimes the application process on an instance hangs. The EC2 status checks of that instance still pass, and the load balancer marks the target as unhealthy. The instance stays in service for days until an engineer terminates it by hand. The company wants to automate the replacement of these instances. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs an AWS Lambda function every minute to terminate the instances that the load balancer reports as unhealthy.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on Elastic Load Balancing health checks for the Auto Scaling group, so that instances that fail the load balancer health check are replaced.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the deregistration delay of the target group, so that in-flight requests finish before the load balancer removes the hung instances.

options.label: D
options.text: Lower the unhealthy threshold of the target group health check, so that the load balancer terminates and replaces the hung instances sooner.

items.stem: A company runs six small web applications in one AWS Region. Each application has its own domain name, its own Amazon EC2 instances and its own Application Load Balancer. Each load balancer has an HTTPS listener on port 443 with an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for its domain. Traffic to every application is low, but the load balancers run all day. Users must keep reaching each application at its current URL. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep one Application Load Balancer for each application, and lower the idle timeout of each load balancer so that unused connections close sooner.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep one Application Load Balancer for each application, and turn off cross-zone load balancing on each target group to avoid data transfer charges.

options.label: C
options.text: Replace the six load balancers with one Network Load Balancer that has six TLS listeners, one listener on a different port for each application.

options.label: D
options.text: Use one Application Load Balancer with one HTTPS listener that holds all six certificates, and add host-header rules that forward to six target groups.

items.stem: A solutions architect reviews the design of a new internet-facing TCP application on Amazon EC2 instances. In the design, a Network Load Balancer has one subnet, in Availability Zone A, and all the instances run in Availability Zone A. The application must be highly available and must keep serving clients if one Availability Zone fails. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create a second Network Load Balancer with a subnet in Availability Zone B, and use Amazon Route 53 failover records to switch clients between the two load balancers.

options.label: B
options.text: Run instances in Availability Zone B as well, for example with an Auto Scaling group that spans both zones and registers its instances with the target group.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on cross-zone load balancing for the target group so that the load balancer node in Availability Zone A can also use targets in other zones.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the instances in Availability Zone A with larger instance types so that the remaining instances can carry the load when one instance fails.

options.label: E
options.text: Give the Network Load Balancer a subnet in Availability Zone B as well, so that it has a load balancer node in each of the two zones.

items.stem: A company hosts three websites, example.com, example.net and example.org, on Amazon EC2 instances behind one Application Load Balancer. Host-based listener rules send the requests of each website to its own target group. The company must now encrypt the traffic in transit between users and the load balancer, and every website must stay on port 443. Each website has its own public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the load balancer with a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on port 443, and install each website's certificate on the instances.

options.label: B
options.text: Create three Application Load Balancers, one per website, each with an HTTPS listener on port 443 and that website's ACM certificate.

options.label: C
options.text: Create HTTPS listeners on ports 443, 8443 and 9443, one per website, and attach that website's ACM certificate to each.

options.label: D
options.text: Create one HTTPS listener on port 443, and add all three ACM certificates to the certificate list of that listener.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances that are registered in an Application Load Balancer target group with the default health check settings. After a release, the application currently answers requests for the path / with an HTTP 302 redirect to a sign-in page. Every target is now marked unhealthy, but users can still use the website. The company must ensure that the health checks show the real state of each target. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the health check protocol of the target group to TCP so that a target counts as healthy when it accepts a connection.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the health check path of the target group to a /health page that returns HTTP 200 when the application can serve requests.

options.label: C
options.text: Make no change, because the load balancer stops sending requests to unhealthy targets, so the health checks already protect the users.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the application so that the path / returns HTTP 200 instead of a redirect, and release the new version to every instance.

items.stem: A company has several VPCs in one AWS Region and a central security VPC. Security policy requires that all traffic into and out of each VPC passes through a fleet of third-party firewall appliances that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The fleet must be scalable as traffic grows, and the company wants to centrally manage the appliances. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Gateway Load Balancer for the appliances in the security VPC, add Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in each VPC, and route traffic to the endpoints.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a separate Gateway Load Balancer and a separate fleet of appliances in each VPC, and route the traffic of each VPC through its own fleet.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer for the appliances in the security VPC, and point every client and application at the DNS name of that load balancer.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer with an AWS WAF web ACL in each VPC, and send all inbound web requests through that load balancer.

items.stem: A company is moving an HTTP web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run across multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region. Business partners call the application from their own networks over the internet. The company needs one entry point in front of the instances that keeps serving requests when an instance fails. Requests for /api/* must go to a separate group of instances. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with one Elastic IP address in each subnet and a TCP listener that forwards all requests to one target group of the instances.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer, associate one Elastic IP address with its node in each subnet, and forward all requests to one target group of the instances.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with one Elastic IP address in each subnet, and register as its target an Application Load Balancer that has a /api/* listener rule.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer with a listener rule that forwards /api/* requests to a second target group and all other requests to the first target group.

items.stem: A company runs an API on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer in one VPC. Listener rules send /orders/* and /reports/* to separate target groups. A large customer now requires a fixed set of IP addresses that it can allow-list in its firewall. The path-based routing must stay in place, and the company uses one AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer that has an Elastic IP address in each subnet, and move the path rules to its listener.

options.label: B
options.text: Associate an Elastic IP address with the Application Load Balancer node in each subnet, and give the customer those addresses to allow-list.

options.label: C
options.text: Launch Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic IP addresses that run reverse proxy software, and have them forward every request to the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with an Elastic IP address in each subnet, and register the existing Application Load Balancer as its target.

items.stem: A company runs a three-tier application in one VPC. The internet-facing web tier runs on Amazon EC2 instances, and users must reach it through one endpoint. The web tier calls the application tier, which also runs on EC2 instances. Each tier must scale on its own. The application tier must be reachable privately from the web tier and must stay unreachable from the internet. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create an internal Application Load Balancer in private subnets, register the application tier instances, and point the web tier's calls at it.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a listener rule to the internet-facing load balancer that forwards /app/* requests to a target group of the application tier instances.

options.label: C
options.text: Give the application tier instances public IP addresses in public subnets so that the internet-facing load balancer can reach them as targets.

options.label: D
options.text: Launch Amazon EC2 instances that run open source proxy software in private subnets, and have them spread the web tier's calls over the application tier.

options.label: E
options.text: Create an internet-facing Application Load Balancer in public subnets, and register the web tier instances in its target group.

items.stem: A company runs a TCP service on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer that was created with default settings. The instances run across multiple Availability Zones: 2 instances in Availability Zone A and 6 instances in Availability Zone B. Client connections are spread evenly over the two load balancer nodes. The 2 instances in Availability Zone A are overloaded, and the other instances are mostly idle. The company must spread connections evenly over all 8 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on cross-zone load balancing for the target group, and accept the charge for data that crosses between Availability Zones.

options.label: B
options.text: Add 2 instances in each Availability Zone, because cross-zone load balancing is already turned on for every type of load balancer.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the routing algorithm of the target group to least outstanding requests so that new connections go to the least busy instances.

options.label: D
options.text: Launch 4 more instances in Availability Zone A, and keep the same number of instances in each zone whenever the fleet changes size.

items.stem: A company runs a file upload service on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Some uploads are long-running and take up to 10 minutes. The target group uses the default deregistration delay. When the group scales in, some uploads that are still in progress on the instances that the group removes fail. The company wants minimal downtime for uploads during scale-in. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the idle timeout of the load balancer to 900 seconds so that connections to the instances stay open during scale-in.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a lifecycle hook to the Auto Scaling group, and run a script on each instance that completes the hook after its uploads finish.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the deregistration delay of the target group to 900 seconds so that in-progress uploads can finish before an instance is removed.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on sticky sessions for the target group so that each user's upload stays on the same instance until the upload is complete.

items.stem: A company's website runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The HTTPS listener uses a certificate that a third-party certificate authority issued and that the company imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Last year the certificate expired, and the website was unavailable until an engineer imported a new certificate. The company wants to automate certificate renewal so that this outage does not happen again. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the imported certificate on the listener, and rely on ACM managed renewal to renew the certificate before it expires.

options.label: B
options.text: Request a public certificate for the domain from ACM, and replace the imported certificate on the HTTPS listener with it.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that buys a new certificate from the third-party authority every year and imports it into ACM.

options.label: D
options.text: Upload the third-party certificate to IAM, and change the HTTPS listener to use the IAM certificate instead of the ACM certificate.

items.stem: A company is moving an HTTP web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run across multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region. Business partners call the application from their own networks over the internet. The company needs one entry point in front of the instances that keeps serving requests when an instance fails. Each partner must allow-list the load balancer's IP addresses, and the addresses must never change. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer with a listener rule that forwards /api/* requests to a second target group and all other requests to the first target group.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with one Elastic IP address in each subnet, and register as its target an Application Load Balancer that has a /api/* listener rule.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer, associate one Elastic IP address with its node in each subnet, and forward all requests to one target group of the instances.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with one Elastic IP address in each subnet and a TCP listener that forwards all requests to one target group of the instances.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in two Availability Zones. Clients connect over HTTPS on port 443 through a new load balancer. The company wants to protect the data in transit on every network hop. The load balancer must route each request to a target group by its URL path. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the connections to a TLS target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

options.label: B
options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the requests to an HTTPS target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

options.label: C
options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on port 443, and forward the connections to a TCP target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

options.label: D
options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the requests to an HTTP target group of the instances on port 80.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application keeps each user's session data in the memory of the instance that served the user's first request. Users are signed out when a later request reaches a different instance. The company wants a fix as soon as possible, with minimal code changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer, and turn on source IP stickiness for the target group of the instances.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on duration-based stickiness for the target group, so that the load balancer sends all requests of a user to the same instance.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the session data in an Amazon ElastiCache cluster that every instance reads and writes, and change the application to use the cluster.

options.label: D
options.text: Run a session database on one new EC2 instance that every web instance reads and writes, and change the application to use that database.

items.stem: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. The instances have public IP addresses and are registered as instance targets of an internet-facing Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on port 443. The load balancer was created years ago without security groups. The instances' security group allows TCP port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The company must restrict access to the instances, and clients must keep reaching the application through a load balancer. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the rule that allows port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, because a Network Load Balancer has no security group that a target rule can reference.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the instances to private subnets without public IP addresses, and keep the rule that allows port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 on the instances.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new Network Load Balancer with a security group, allow port 443 on the instances only from that security group, and move clients to it.

options.label: D
options.text: Associate a new security group with the existing Network Load Balancer, and allow port 443 on the instances only from that security group.

items.stem: A company serves a website through an Application Load Balancer that has an HTTPS listener on port 443 with an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate. The load balancer has no other listener. Users who enter the website address with HTTP in the browser receive an error. The company wants these users to reach the HTTPS site, so that all requests are encrypted in transit. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add an HTTP listener on port 80 whose default action returns a fixed response that asks users to enter the HTTPS address in the browser.

options.label: B
options.text: Add an HTTP listener on port 80 whose default action redirects every request to HTTPS on port 443 with a permanent HTTP 301 response.

options.label: C
options.text: Add an HTTP listener on port 80 that forwards requests to the instances, and change the application code to return a redirect to HTTPS.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a second Application Load Balancer with an HTTP listener on port 80, and point a second DNS name for the website at that load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Cross-zone load balancing is turned off for the target group, and zonal shift is turned on for the load balancer. During an incident, responses from the instances in one Availability Zone become slow, but those instances still pass their health checks. The company must move traffic away from that Availability Zone as soon as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a new Application Load Balancer in the two healthy Availability Zones, register their instances, and point the DNS record of the website at it.

options.label: B
options.text: Start a zonal shift in Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) for the load balancer, away from the Availability Zone with the slow instances.

options.label: C
options.text: Wait for the target group health checks to mark the slow instances as unhealthy, so that the load balancer stops routing requests to them.

options.label: D
options.text: Deregister the instances in that Availability Zone from the target group one at a time, and register them again after the incident ends.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in two Availability Zones. Clients connect over HTTPS on port 443 through a new load balancer. The company wants to protect the data in transit on every network hop. Each instance must decrypt the client traffic with its own certificate and private key. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the requests to an HTTPS target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

options.label: B
options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on port 443, and forward the connections to a TCP target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

options.label: C
options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the requests to an HTTP target group of the instances on port 80.

options.label: D
options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener that has an ACM certificate, and forward the connections to a TLS target group of the instances, which hold certificates.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application keeps each user's session data in the memory of the instance that served the user's first request. Users are signed out when a later request reaches a different instance. Users must keep their sessions when an instance is terminated, so the web tier must become stateless and scalable. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the session data in an Amazon ElastiCache cluster that every instance reads and writes, and change the application to use the cluster.

options.label: B
options.text: Run a session database on one new EC2 instance that every web instance reads and writes, and change the application to use that database.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on duration-based stickiness for the target group, so that the load balancer sends all requests of a user to the same instance.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer, and turn on source IP stickiness for the target group of the instances.
